source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: A creep box gives piglets a warm, dry, protected place to sleep away from the sow, reducing the risk of piglets being crushed, and is a cheaper alternative to an expensive farrowing crate. It is a simple structure with a floor, roof, and three solid walls, with an opening in the front wall (or no front wall at all) large enough for piglets to move in and out. For 10 piglets: height 50–70cm (with the front opening 30–40cm high), depth (front to back) 0.5 metre, width 1 metre. Add soft bedding such as rice straw, banana leaves, or dry grass to the floor. Place piglets in the box as soon as they've been suckled by the sow so they get used to sleeping there.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
